title: Non-vanishing of L^p de Rham cohomology for the Iwasawa AN groups, via a quantitative non-vanishing criterion and a case-by-case root-subset construction
difficulty_reason: 扣去 Pansu 的 L^p 消失/非消失、Bourdon–Rémy 的度区间与 Poincaré 对偶、Helgason Table VI 与 Bourbaki Planche 的根数据、É. Cartan 的简单实群分类（简单实 Lie 群清单）、附录所引 [Pa95]/[IL93]/[BT82]/Sequeira 的双复形行/列形变收缩（本批作外部标准输入扣除，见 excluded_cores）、Humphreys 的上三角化之后，保留三段作者自写承重。其一为判据（命题 3.2，1074–1088；其证明 1112–1146 在原文中排在推论 3.4 的证明之后）：把非消失归约为三条可检验假设（J 的主性、权为实、紧支撑原函数），对每个 j∈J 用沿 Y_j 流的历史积分 θ_j 造出原式，再把 ‖C*_{exp X}(θ_j)‖ 的指数衰减与引理 3.1 的插值（999–1004，证明 1006–1055）对接，在 1<p<h/W_{n-1} 上保住闭性并得 H̄^l_dR 非零。其二为组合命题到判据的接口（引理 5.1，1313–1317；证明 1322–1339）：(i) 直接把 2ρ_G 写成 Ψ 的组合，(ii) 逼出 X=0，(iii′) 的“至多一对坏和”由 §4 两条引理供给紧支撑函数（1157–1160/1200–1207，证明 1162–1198/1209–1214，后者以导降中心列长度作归纳）。其三为逐型构造 Ψ 并逐条验证 (i)–(iii)（1445–1546 的 B_l/C_l/BC_l/D_l，1552–1635 的 E_6/E_7/E_8/F_4/G_2，以及 5.3 的 A_l 命题 1653–1672 与证明 1674–1735，含 5.2 的线性代数引理 1368–1379/证明 1381–1428）；A_l 偶 l 必须把 (iii) 放宽为 (iii′)，作者在 1663–1670 显式给出该放宽，这是实质弱化而非记号。最后 1740–1747 把各型合起来证定理 D。此处不因“L^p 上同调”“Iwasawa”或群名赋难度。只保留作者实际证明、引用、略证和省略部分；不补证明、不修式、不裁定真假。

exact_primary_comparisons.title: Quasi-isometry invariance of continuous regular-representation Lp cohomology for unimodular locally compact second-countable groups

primary.theorem: theo intro-thm1 (printed as Theorem 1.1 of the AHL paper)

exact_primary_comparisons.statement:
10: \begin{theo}\label{intro-thm1}
11: Let $G_1$, $G_2$ be locally compact second countable groups, equip\-ped with left-invariant proper metrics. Every quasi-isometry $F: G_1 \to G_2$ induces canonically an isomorphism of graded topological vector spaces
12: \[
13: F ^*\!: {\rm H}^*_{\ct} \bigl(G_2, L^p(G_2) \bigr) \to {\rm H}^*_{\ct} \bigl(G_1, L^p(G_1) \bigr).
14: \]
15: The same holds for the reduced cohomology.
16: \end{theo}

secondary_statements_read.label: coro cont_asymp_cor
secondary_statements_read.statement:
343: \begin{coro}\label{cont_asymp_cor}
344: Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be locally compact second countable topological groups, equipped with left-invariant proper metrics and let $F : G_1 \to G_2$ be a quasi-isometry. Then $F$ induces a homotopy equivalence between the complexes
345: \[
346: C^*\bigl(G_1, L^p(G_1)\bigr)^{G_1}\quad\text{and}\quad C^*\bigl(G_2, L^p(G_2)\bigr)^{G_2}. 
347: \]
348: Moreover the associated isomorphism of graded topological vector spaces
349: \[
350: F ^* :{\rm H}^*_{\ct} \bigl(G_2, L^p(G_2) \bigr) \to {\rm H}^*_{\ct} \bigl(G_1, L^p(G_1) \bigr)
351: \] 
352: depends only the bounded perturbation class of $F$.
353: \end{coro}
secondary_statements_read.read_because: The old record's equivalent_precise_statement range [450,460] points at this corollary, not at the introduction theorem; reading it is what makes the object-level comparison with JEP232 sound rather than title-level.

exact_primary_comparisons.owner_comparison: Old counted claim (Theorem 1.1): for locally compact second countable G_1, G_2 with left-invariant proper metrics, every quasi-isometry F induces a canonical isomorphism of graded topological vector spaces F^*: H^*_ct(G_2,L^p(G_2)) -> H^*_ct(G_1,L^p(G_1)), and the same for reduced cohomology; Corollary cont_asymp_cor adds the homotopy equivalence of the complexes C^*(G_i,L^p(G_i))^{G_i} and the dependence of the isomorphism only on the bounded perturbation class of F. This is an INVARIANCE statement: it says the cohomology does not change under quasi-isometry. JEP232 c1 (Section 4, Lemma 4.1 + Proposition 4.2 + Corollary 4.4) is a NON-VANISHING criterion for R = B x| H with H a Heintze group: it constructs a specific closed form psi = pi^*(f vol) from a compactly supported f whose orbital integrals along every Y_j vanish, controls its Psi^{p,n}(H) norm by an inf-interpolation between the N-scale and the H-scale, and requires p-integrability along the b-directions; the conclusion is L^p reduced H^l_dR(R) != {0}. JEP232 c2 (Section 6, Lemma 6.1 + 6.2 + Proposition 6.3 + Theorem D) is a purely combinatorial root-system construction solving the (i)(ii)(iii)/(iii') subset problem for every Cartan type, with no cohomology in it at all. JEP232 c3 (Appendix, Theorem A.1 = Theorem 7.6 with Props A.4/A.5/A.8) is a comparison of asymptotic and de Rham L^p-cohomology on a manifold uniformly diffeomorphic to R^D via a double complex that deformation-retracts to both ends. Object, premises and conclusion differ in all three cases: 2639 quantifies over an arbitrary quasi-isometry between two groups and concludes an isomorphism; c1 quantifies over a specific solvable group built from a Heintze group and concludes non-vanishing of one degree; c2 has no cohomology; c3 quantifies over a manifold and concludes a homotopy equivalence of two complexes on the SAME manifold. What the old item supplies to JEP232 is a cited input (the invariance theorem, used for Theorem A and for the Section 7 isomorphisms), not a shared core.

editorial_notes: Reuse the complete fixed work, index and PDF once; source author mathematics unchanged; no per-entry full native copies.

The criterion (Proposition 3.2) is conditional: it presupposes dominance of J, real eigenweights, and an integrable compactly-supported primitive; the unit does not claim non-vanishing for a general solvable group outside conditions (nC)+(nT).

The degree is l = rk_R(G) (the rank of the solvable factor in the Iwasawa decomposition); the p range is the author's 1<p<h/W_{n-1} for the interpolation Lemma 3.1 and p>h/w_l for Corollary 3.4, while Theorem A only says 'large enough p>1'. No claim is made for small p.

Theorem D covers only the groups AN arising in Iwasawa decompositions KAN of semisimple real Lie groups with finite center; the reduction to Theorem A lives in section 'ss - ss and QI' (L322) and uses Poincare duality and [BR], which are not re-proved here.
Vanishing in degrees above l (Theorem A(ii)) is not part of this unit: it is proved through [BR] and appears only as a cited input.

For type A_l with l even the author only obtains (iii'), i.e. at most one exceptional pair with beta+beta' in Phi (1296-1302, 1663-1670); the merged unit must be recorded with the relaxed condition and must not be restated as satisfying (iii).

The appendix (1980-2251) re-proves Pansu's theorem as an external standard input; it is a cited dependency of this unit, not an additional independent core and not a licence to claim the author's own mechanism.
Non-vanishing statements are about reduced cohomology where the author writes an overline (Theorem A(i), Corollary 3.4); the unreduced statement must not be substituted.

source_conditions: The criterion (Proposition 3.2) is conditional: it presupposes dominance of J, real eigenweights, and an integrable compactly-supported primitive; the unit does not claim non-vanishing for a general solvable group outside conditions (nC)+(nT).

The degree is l = rk_R(G) (the rank of the solvable factor in the Iwasawa decomposition); the p range is the author's 1<p<h/W_{n-1} for the interpolation Lemma 3.1 and p>h/w_l for Corollary 3.4, while Theorem A only says 'large enough p>1'. No claim is made for small p.

Theorem D covers only the groups AN arising in Iwasawa decompositions KAN of semisimple real Lie groups with finite center; the reduction to Theorem A lives in section 'ss - ss and QI' (L322) and uses Poincare duality and [BR], which are not re-proved here.
Vanishing in degrees above l (Theorem A(ii)) is not part of this unit: it is proved through [BR] and appears only as a cited input.

For type A_l with l even the author only obtains (iii'), i.e. at most one exceptional pair with beta+beta' in Phi (1296-1302, 1663-1670); the merged unit must be recorded with the relaxed condition and must not be restated as satisfying (iii).

The appendix (1980-2251) re-proves Pansu's theorem as an external standard input; it is a cited dependency of this unit, not an additional independent core and not a licence to claim the author's own mechanism.
Non-vanishing statements are about reduced cohomology where the author writes an overline (Theorem A(i), Corollary 3.4); the unreduced statement must not be substituted.

(1) jep232-c1 and jep232-c2 are merged into one independent core at H3, as the producer's candidate_merge_suggestion recommends: the criterion alone yields nothing for semisimple groups without the Psi construction, the construction without the criterion is a combinatorial identity, and the two interlock directly in the proof of Theorem D (1740-1747); the per-type verification is the classification discussion of one and the same combinatorial proposition. (2) jep232-c3 (appendix, 1980-2251) is not counted as an independent candidate: the double-complex strategy and both deformation retractions are attributed by the author to [Pa95] and [IL93], with a detailed proof in Sequeira and the same form in [BT82]; per COMMON_RULES only independent propositions with a concrete non-routine H2/H3 core reason count as qualified, and the producer itself recorded difficulty_confidence=borderline_H2_H1 with the explicit caveat that under a strict new-mechanism standard it should be H1 or not counted.
